  • Cantus: Base text M (critical edition, Sources). Compared note by note with M's lyrics.
  • Altus: Base text M. Compared note by note with M's lyrics; bars 5–6 follow N (critical note).
  • Tenor: Base text T, the 1611 print. T places its text loosely; its words fall where M's do (critical edition, Underlay), so T's syllables are read from M's Tenor: as M = as T. ⟨ ⟩ passages are T's ij, supplied.
  • Bassus: Base text M. Compared note by note with M's lyrics.
  • Tenor: the 1611 print (T) gives the words under the notes but loosely and writes ij four times (bars 21–22, 33–35, 35–37, 43–45); the edition reads T's placement from M (critical edition, Underlay).
  • Cantus, Altus, Bassus: compared with Marchesano's edition (M, music/src_M_Marchesano.xml) note by note. The departures found are the ones the critical notes give: C 38–39, A 5–6 (as N), A 36–37, T 38–40.
  • Ours: supplied for ij ⟨ ⟩: 24; changed from M: 6.

Key words in context

The text as the edition prints it, a line per row, with the edition's translation. Confirmed key words count (gate key_word); proposed ones have no effect until confirmed in editions.yaml. The stressed syllable is underlined. Text from editions/vox-in-rama/vox-in-rama-performance.lytex.

TextTranslation
Vox in Rama audita est,A voice was heard in Rama,
ploratus et ululatus:weeping and wailing:
Rachel plorans filios suos,Rachel weeping for her children,
et noluit consolari,and she would not be comforted,
quia non sunt.because they are not.

Against the tactus

Syncopation declaimed by two or more voices together, or a hemiola-like chain of syncopated semibreves in one voice. Inside a span U210 also accepts the displaced pulse as a beat, and U201 and U202 count half (gate against_tactus).
